say: Shampoo, Conditioning Shampoo and Hair Conditioner. This is module 3 of the course.
Hair products sell on feel, so today we make all three and test them on real hair.

shots.label: Shampoo for textured hair
say: Afro-textured hair tends to be dry, because scalp oil doesn't travel easily along the coils.
So the shampoo in these bottles should clean the scalp well but stop short of squeaky.
Compared with the hand wash, we raise CAPB from 5% to 7% and add panthenol, provitamin B5, to help hair hold water.

shots.label: Small ingredients on 0.1 g scale

card.title: Ifeoma's 12 kg shampoo
card.note: Active matter 11.9%. Plus EDTA 12 g, preservative 96 g

say: Ifeoma in Owerri checked her assistant's sheet before her first 12 kg batch.
The non-water lines came to 3,084 g, so water had to be 8,916 g. It matched.
Notice the panthenol going onto the small scale. Tiny amounts need the precise scale, not the platform one.

shots.label: Water and EDTA, then SLES
say: In the bucket, dissolve EDTA in the water, keeping about 10% back for brine.
Dissolve the SLES slowly with gentle stirring, then add CAPB, glycerin and panthenol.
Premix the fragrance with a little CAPB and add it with the preservative.

shots.label: Target pH 5 to 6
say: Now the strip. Shampoo should be slightly acidic, about 5 to 6. Adjust with the 1% sample method from module 1.

shots.label: Salt brine after a step test
say: Thicken with salt brine after a step test, a little thicker than your hand wash. Then rest it overnight and check it before filling.

shots.label: Rinse eyes with clean water
say: Most shampoos sting the eyes. Your label must say: avoid contact with eyes, and if contact occurs, rinse well with clean water, like this.
Don't write tear-free, anti-dandruff or hair growth unless you have the testing and NAFDAC approval.

shots.label: Guar slurry into stirring water
say: For a 2-in-1, a small amount of cationic polymer leaves a thin film on hair when you rinse.
The powder lumps if you tip it in. So Kemi stirred her 30 g of guar into the glycerin first, then poured the slurry into stirring water.
After 30 minutes, smooth and slightly thick, she carried on with the normal shampoo method.

shots.label: Standard versus 2-in-1

card.title: Wet-combing test
card.note: Course example; repeat on three days and average

say: Prove it works. Wash two identical hair bundles, one with each bottle, then count comb strokes while wet.
Never make a 2-in-1 by pouring a conditioner or quat disinfectant into shampoo. It goes cloudy and separates.

shots.label: Weigh the empty pot first
say: Now the conditioner, a cream that doesn't foam. Weigh phase A into a steel pot, and write down the empty pot weight first.
Phase B, the waxes, goes in a second pot. BTMS-50 pastilles both emulsify and condition.

shots.label: Long sleeves, heat-resistant gloves
shots.banner: Melt wax in a double boiler, not on flame
say: Melted wax at 75 degrees causes serious burns and sticks to skin.
Wear long sleeves, closed shoes and heat-resistant gloves. Turn pot handles inwards and keep children out.

shots.label: Phase B poured into phase A
say: Both pots heat in water baths to about 75 degrees. Hold them 10 to 15 minutes so all the wax melts.
Watch: phase B pours into phase A, with short bursts of a stick blender for 2 to 3 minutes.
Keep stirring as it cools. See it turn thick and creamy between about 50 and 40 degrees.

shots.label: Phase C: preservative, fragrance
say: Only below 40 degrees do the preservative and fragrance go in. They are heat-sensitive.

shots.label: Cool running water for burns
say: If hot wax touches skin, cool the burn under cool running water for at least 20 minutes, and seek medical care for anything larger than a small area.
Back on the scale. Ngozi's pot weighed 1,800 g empty, so with 5 kg of cream it should read 6,800 g. It read 6,640 g.
She stirred back 160 g of boiled, cooled water. Rest 24 hours, check pH is about 4 to 5.5, then fill wide-neck jars.
Now go through the lessons below. Make your test shampoo and user panel, your 2-in-1 comparison, and your first 1 kg conditioner with a temperature log.
